content.title: About
content.content: Dry white cheese (queso seco) is a traditional Spanish and Latin American product made from cow’s milk. It has a hard texture, pale‑white color and a mildly salty, nutty flavor. It is commonly used as a topping for dishes, in salads, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dry cheese is traditionally produced in regions with a dry climate, allowing it to be stored without refrigeration.
In Mexico queso seco is often served with tacos and enchiladas, while in Spain it appears in tapas.
The cheese is aged for at least 3‑6 months, giving it its characteristic aroma.
It is usually grated on a coarse grater so it adheres well to foods.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: The cheese provides a high amount of calcium, essential for bone and tooth health.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Dry cheese supplies high‑quality animal protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Low lactose content
items.content: Extended aging reduces lactose levels, making the cheese more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk proteins may experience reactions when consuming the cheese.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Dry cheese is often salty; those with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Like most cheeses, it is calorie‑dense, so portions should be moderate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grate the dry white cheese over pasta, add it to salads, sprinkle on soups, use it in taco fillings, or simply enjoy small pieces as a snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep it refrigerated, where it will keep its flavor for up to 6 months. Discard if mold or off‑odors develop.
